@graph.name: Straight Conveying
@graph.description: Straight conveying systems are the powered roller, belt and modular belt sections that carry cases, cartons, trays and totes along a straight path between machines. In lines from TRF Industrial Automation, they form the backbone of the TRFIntraflow platform, engineered together with transfers, accumulation, routing and controls as one system.

mainEntity.name: Can Roller, Belt and Modular Belt Conveyors Be Combined in One Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many lines use more than one type, because each segment has a different job. TRF selects the module for each position and connects all of them to one control concept, so speed, start and stop follow the state of the whole line. The plant receives a single engineered system rather than a mix of independent sections from different suppliers.

mainEntity.name: Can a Single Supplier Engineer, Build and Install My Entire Conveyor System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. With TRFIntraflow, engineering, manufacturing, controls, assembly, integration and commissioning are managed within one coordinated TRF delivery model, from concept to startup. The same partner can also supply the case packers and palletizers at both ends of the conveyors, so the interfaces between them are defined once, in one project.

mainEntity.name: How Does Straight Conveying Reduce Manual Case Handling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Straight conveying carries cases under control from the case packer to the palletizer, so people do not have to move, turn or clear cases by hand between machines. Sensors and controls keep spacing and speed matched to both ends of the line, which supports steady throughput and less repetitive lifting.

mainEntity.name: Which Industries Use Straight Conveying Systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any plant that packs product into cases, cartons, trays or totes and moves them to a palletizer or a warehouse. TRFIntraflow serves mid-sized and large manufacturers in food processing, beverage, CPG, protein, frozen food, pet food, personal care and industrial sectors. The full list is on the industries page.
